instructions:
# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

## Hindi (hi)

Script: Devanagari. Used in UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, HP, Uttarakhand,
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

## Gujarati (gu)

Script: Gujarati. Used in Gujarat, and spoken in Dadra & Nagar Haveli and
Daman & Diu.
Tone: everyday spoken Gujarati.
Words: ઓનલાઇન, ફોર્મ, પોર્ટલ, લૉગિન, આધાર, બેંક, મોબાઇલ, OTP, હેલ્પલાઇન, સર્ટિફિકેટ / દાખલો,
ડાઉનલોડ, અપલોડ.
UI: અરજી કરો, સબમિટ કરો, આગળ, પાછળ, શોધો, શેર કરો, સેટિંગ્સ, ભાષા, મદદ.
Offices: મામલતદાર, તલાટી, ગ્રામ પંચાયત, કલેક્ટર, તાલુકા પંચાયત.
Gender: જાતિ is caste; use લિંગ. Money: રૂ. 6,000; રૂ. 8 લાખ. September: સપ્ટેમ્બર.

## Marathi (mr)

Script: Devanagari. Used in Maharashtra, and widely in Goa.
Tone: everyday Marathi as spoken in Maharashtra.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बँक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन, दाखला / सर्टिफिकेट,
डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: अर्ज करा, सबमिट करा, पुढे, मागे, शोधा, शेअर करा, सेटिंग्ज, भाषा, मदत.
Offices: तहसीलदार, तलाठी, ग्रामपंचायत, जिल्हाधिकारी (कलेक्टर), आपले सरकार सेवा केंद्र.
Gender: लिंग. Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सप्टेंबर.

## Bengali (bn)

Script: Bengali. Used in West Bengal and Tripura, and in Assam's Barak Valley
and the Andamans.
Tone: everyday spoken Bengali (চলিত ভাষা), not সাধু ভাষা.
Words: অনলাইন, ফর্ম, পোর্টাল, লগইন, আধার, ব্যাংক, মোবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, সার্টিফিকেট,
ডাউনলোড, আপলোড.
UI: আবেদন করুন, জমা দিন, পরবর্তী, পিছনে, খুঁজুন, শেয়ার করুন, সেটিংস, ভাষা, সাহায্য.
Offices: বিডিও অফিস, গ্রাম পঞ্চায়েত, তহসিলদার, জেলাশাসক (কালেক্টর), দুয়ারে সরকার.
Gender: লিঙ্গ. Money: 6,000 টাকা; 8 লাখ টাকা. September: সেপ্টেম্বর.

items.t: Get the disability certificate in hand before anything else. The Chief Medical Officer's board at the district hospital assesses free of charge on fixed weekly days — ask the hospital's disability desk for the day. The certificate must show 80 per cent or more under the current rules, and 40 per cent or more once the new guidelines are issued.
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY, farmer pension)
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (run with LIC and CSC)

A pension of Rs.3,000 a month from age 60 for small and marginal farmers who join between 18 and 40. You pay Rs.55 to Rs.200 a month, depending on your age when you join, and the government adds the same amount. The monthly amount can be cut automatically from your PM-Kisan money. You join at a Common Service Centre (CSC) with your Aadhaar and bank passbook.
Rs.3,000 a month pension from age 60; Rs.1,500 family pension to the spouse
Small and marginal farmers with up to 2 hectares (about 5 acres) of cultivable land in their own name in the land records
Age 18 to 40 years when joining; you pay every month until you turn 60
Not for people already in NPS, ESIC or EPFO, or who joined PM Shram Yogi Maandhan or PM Vyapari Maandhan
Not for income-tax payers, government or PSU employees (Class IV / Group D staff can join), doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs and architects in practice, or holders of constitutional posts
You need an Aadhaar card and a savings bank account
Savings bank passbook or cheque with IFSC (the PM-Kisan account if you want the amount cut from PM-Kisan)
Land record showing land up to 2 hectares in your name
Name and date of birth of your spouse and of the nominee
First month's contribution in cash (Rs.55 to Rs.200)
Maandhan (PM-KMY)

At your nearest Common Service Centre (CSC). Take your Aadhaar card, bank passbook or cheque, land record and spouse and nominee details, and pay the first month's contribution in cash to the operator (VLE). Joining is free; the enrolment-cum-auto-debit form is printed there for you to sign.
The operator checks it with your fingerprint, so you must come yourself.
Name as on Aadhaar
Ganesh Patil
Exactly as printed on the Aadhaar card.
Date of birth as on Aadhaar
Your age on this date decides your monthly amount. At 29 it is Rs.100 a month.
Messages about your contribution and pension come here.
Use the account where PM-Kisan money comes if you want the amount cut from it.
Spouse details
Sunanda Patil, 02-11-1999
Your wife or husband. They get half the pension if you die after 60.
Nominee details
Sunanda Patil (wife)
Who gets your savings if you die before the pension starts and your spouse does not continue.
Land details
Village Wadgaon, Survey 88, 1.2 hectares
From your land record. The total must not be more than 2 hectares.
Pay from PM-Kisan benefit
Choose Yes to have the contribution taken from your PM-Kisan instalments, so you never miss a payment.
Monthly contribution
Rs.100 (government adds Rs.100)
Worked out by the system from your age. You can also choose to pay every 3, 4 or 6 months.
Go to the nearest Common Service Centre with your Aadhaar, bank passbook, land record and spouse and nominee details.
The operator checks your Aadhaar with your fingerprint and fills in your bank, mobile, land, spouse and nominee details. The system shows your monthly amount.
Pay the first month's contribution in cash to the operator.
Sign the enrolment-cum-auto-debit form that is printed. The operator scans and uploads it.
You get your Kisan Pension Account Number (KPAN) and a printed Kisan card on the spot. Keep it safe.
From then on, the amount is cut automatically from your bank account or PM-Kisan money. If you leave within 10 years, you get back your own share with savings bank interest.
At age 60, LIC starts paying Rs.3,000 a month into your bank account. After your death, your spouse gets Rs.1,500 a month.
1800-3000-3468 (PM-KMY / CSC) / 14434 (Maandhan helpline)
Pradhan Mantri Parivar Labh Yojana (National Family Benefit Scheme, NFBS)
Ministry of Rural Development — National Social Assistance Programme (Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana)

A one-time payment of Rs.20,000 to a poor (BPL) family when its main earning member dies between the ages of 18 and 59, from illness, accident or any other cause. A woman who runs the home counts as a breadwinner too. The money goes to the family member who, after a local inquiry, becomes the new head of the household. This is the old National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS), renamed Pradhan Mantri Parivar Labh Yojana by the Cabinet on 14 October 2026 with the benefit unchanged, so local offices may still use the old name.
Rs.20,000 one-time payment to the family, into the bank account
The family is below the poverty line (BPL) on the state's list. An eligible poor family missing from the list should still be considered
The person who died was the main earner of the household. A woman who looked after the home also counts
The death happened when that person was more than 18 and less than 60 years old
Any cause of death counts: illness, accident or anything else
Paid once for each such death, to the surviving member found to be the new head of the household (spouse, minor children, unmarried daughters and dependent parents make up the household)
Death certificate of the breadwinner from the Registrar of Births and Deaths
Age proof of the person who died (birth or school certificate, Aadhaar or voter ID) showing an age between 18 and 59
BPL ration card, or the family's BPL list number
First page of the bank or post-office passbook in the applicant's own name
FIR and post-mortem report, if the death was an accident
Residence proof and two passport-size photographs
Income certificate or legal heir / family certificate, where the state asks for it

The office your state has named for this scheme: usually the Tehsil or SDM office, the Block Development Office, or the District / Tehsil Social Welfare Officer. In a village the Gram Panchayat secretary can take it and forward it; in a town, the municipal office. Most offices give their own form free; the government's model form is Annexe III (page 47) of the NSAP guidelines PDF. Take the filled form with the death certificate, the age proof of the person who died, the BPL ration card, your Aadhaar, your passbook and two photos, plus the FIR and post-mortem report for an accidental death. Some states also take this application online through their e-District or social welfare portal, or at a CSC.

The age must be more than 18 and less than 60. Take it from the age proof you attach, not from memory.
Date and Cause of Death
14-07-2026, road accident
Date as on the death certificate. For an accident, attach the FIR and post-mortem report.
The family member who is now head of the household, usually the widow or widower.
Father's / Husband's Name of the Applicant
Late Ramesh Kumar Paswan
As on your Aadhaar card.
Relationship of the Applicant with the Deceased

Wife, husband, son, daughter, father or mother.

Where the family lives now.
BPL Details (Survey Year, Family ID, Member ID) / Ration Card No.

Copy from the BPL ration card or the BPL list kept at the Panchayat.

Everyone in the household who depended on the person who died.
Aadhaar and Bank Account of the Applicant

Get the death registered and collect the death certificate from the Panchayat or municipal Registrar. Nothing can be sanctioned without it.
Collect the free form at the Tehsil, Block or Social Welfare office (or the Gram Panchayat), fill it and attach the documents.
Get the verification part signed by the Sarpanch or ward member, submit the form at the named office, and take a dated receipt with an inward number.

A verification officer checks the facts, normally within two weeks. The case is then placed before the Gram Sabha or ward sabha and sent to the sanctioning officer (BDO, Tehsildar / SDM or District Social Welfare Officer).
The guidelines say the decision should come within 60 days of applying. You get a sanction order and Rs.20,000 is sent to your bank account.
If it is rejected, the reason must be given to you in writing. Appeal to the appellate officer your state names, usually the SDM or a district officer.

No national toll-free line: Block Development Office, Tehsil / SDM office or District Social Welfare Officer. Unresolved complaints: NSAP Division, Ministry of Rural Development 011-24663519, or CPGRAMS (pgportal.gov.in)
Pradhan Mantri Vidhawa Pension Yojana (formerly IGNWPS)

A monthly pension for widows aged 40 and above in below-poverty-line households. It was called the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) until the Union Cabinet renamed it on 14 October 2026, as part of the Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana (formerly NSAP); the amount and rules stay the same. The Centre pays a fixed share and the state adds its own top-up. The pension stops if the widow remarries, and converts to the old-age pension once she turns 60 in states that run both.
Pradhan Mantri Vridhavastha Pension Yojana (formerly IGNOAPS)

A monthly pension for people aged 60 and above who belong to a below-poverty-line household. It was called the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) until the Union Cabinet renamed it on 14 October 2026, as part of the Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana (formerly the National Social Assistance Programme, NSAP); the amount and rules stay the same. The Centre pays a fixed share and almost every state adds a top-up, so the amount that actually reaches the bank account is usually larger than the central figure.
DAY-NRLM Self-Help Group (Aajeevika SHG / Lakhpati Didi)
Ministry of Rural Development — Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission, through each State Rural Livelihoods Mission

Women from poor village families join a self-help group (SHG) of 10 to 20 women who save a small sum every week and lend to each other. A group that runs well gets a Revolving Fund of Rs.20,000–30,000, can borrow up to Rs.2.5 lakh from the Community Investment Fund through its village federation, and gets bank loans without collateral at a low rate. Members are trained and supported to take up dairy, farming or small businesses, with the aim of earning Rs.1 lakh a year as a 'Lakhpati Didi'. About 10 crore women are in these groups; you join through your village organisation or the block office of your state's livelihood mission, such as JEEViKA in Bihar, UMED in Maharashtra or Kudumbashree in Kerala.
Revolving Fund Rs.20,000–30,000 per group, up to Rs.2.5 lakh CIF per group, bank loans at 7% up to Rs.3 lakh
Women from poor rural households, picked out by the village itself or from the SECC deprivation list
One woman from each household, in one group
A group has 10 to 20 members (fewer in hilly or remote areas and in groups of persons with disabilities)
The group must meet, save, lend, repay on time and keep books regularly (the 'Panchasutra') to get the Revolving Fund
Community Investment Fund and bank loans follow once the group is graded by the mission and the bank
Lakhpati Didi support usually goes to members who have been in an SHG for at least two years and have used the CIF
Aadhaar card of each member
Passport-size photographs of the members
Savings account opened in the group's name, with a resolution signed by all members
ID proof of the three office-bearers who will operate the group account
Bank passbook of each member
Group meeting register and savings and loan ledger, kept by the group's bookkeeper

Speak to the Community Resource Person (CRP, the SHG didi or sakhi) or the Village Organisation in your village, or go to the Block Mission Management Unit of your State Rural Livelihoods Mission at the block office. Join an existing group or form a new one with 10–20 women from nearby households; the CRP helps open the group's bank account at the nearest branch and enters the group in the mission's records. Take your Aadhaar, photographs and bank passbook.

Meet the CRP or Village Organisation. With 10–20 women from nearby poor households, hold the first meeting, name the group and fix the weekly saving.
Open a savings account in the group's name with the three office-bearers as signatories; the CRP records the group and each member with the mission.
Meet every week, save, lend among yourselves, repay on time and keep the books for about three months.
The group gets the Revolving Fund of Rs.20,000–30,000 in its account and joins the Village Organisation.
Through the village federation the group can borrow from the Community Investment Fund, up to Rs.2.5 lakh per SHG, against the members' credit plan.
The bank gives the group loans without collateral, at 7% for loans up to Rs.3 lakh, with bigger loans after each repayment. Members use them for dairy, farming, shops or other work.
Members are trained under the Lakhpati Didi plan, and the CRP records household income in the Digital Aajeevika Register.
Block Mission Management Unit of your State Rural Livelihoods Mission; DAY-NRLM, Ministry of Rural Development 011-23461708; Lakhpati Didi portal support 0120-5202521 (Mon–Sat, 9 am–6 pm)
Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
National Health Mission, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare

Cash given to a mother who delivers her baby in a government hospital, or in an approved private hospital if she is from a BPL, SC or ST family. The village ASHA helps you register, takes you for check-ups and gets the payment made. Under a separate scheme (JSSK) the delivery itself is free, even a caesarean, along with medicines, food and the ambulance. JSY money is extra, paid into your bank account after the delivery.
Rs.1,400 (village) or Rs.1,000 (town) in low-performing states; Rs.700 or Rs.600 elsewhere

In Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Assam, Uttarakhand and Jammu & Kashmir: every pregnant woman who delivers in a government hospital or health centre
In all other states: women from BPL, SC or ST families who deliver in a government hospital or health centre
In every state: BPL, SC or ST women who deliver in an approved (accredited) private hospital
There is no age limit and no limit on the number of children for a hospital delivery
BPL women who deliver at home get Rs.500

BPL ration card, or SC/ST caste certificate (needed outside the low-performing states, and for a private hospital delivery)

At the government hospital or health centre where you deliver: before going home, hand your MCP card, Aadhaar copy, bank passbook copy and (where needed) the BPL ration card or caste certificate to the JSY desk or labour-room staff. Your village ASHA can collect and submit them for you. For a home delivery, give them to the ASHA or the ANM at the sub-centre.

Go for the pregnancy check-ups written on the card. Ask for the BPL or caste certificate to be noted if you live outside the low-performing states.

Before leaving the hospital, give your Aadhaar, bank passbook copy and MCP card to the JSY desk or labour-room staff, or hand them to the ASHA.
The hospital enters your claim. The money is sent straight to your bank account, usually within a few weeks.
If it has not come in a month, ask the ASHA or the hospital's JSY clerk, or call 104 with your MCP card number.
104 (state health helpline) / 102 (free ambulance for pregnant women) / 108
Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY / Sukanya Account)
Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance; run through India Post and authorised banks

A savings account in a girl's name that pays one of the highest safe interest rates in the country, 8.2% a year for October to December 2026, completely tax-free. A parent opens it before the girl turns 10, at a post office or authorised bank, with as little as Rs.250, and keeps depositing for 15 years; the account matures 21 years after opening. Half the money can be taken out after she turns 18 for her studies. Rs.1,000 a month for 15 years grows to about Rs.5.5 lakh at today's rate.
8.2% tax-free interest; deposit Rs.250 to Rs.1.5 lakh a year
Girl child below 10 years of age, resident in India
Opened by the girl's parent or legal guardian; accounts opened by grandparents must be moved to a parent's name
One account per girl, and at most two girls per family (a third only for twins or triplets)
Minimum Rs.250 and maximum Rs.1.5 lakh in a financial year, paid for 15 years from opening
A year without the minimum deposit can be made good by paying Rs.250 for that year plus Rs.50 penalty

Fill in the girl's details from her birth certificate and your own as parent, and attach copies of the birth certificate, your Aadhaar and PAN, with photos.
Hand it in with the first deposit. The clerk checks the originals and gives you a passbook with the account number.
Deposit at least Rs.250 every financial year for 15 years, at the counter, through the India Post or IPPB app, or by standing instruction.
Interest, 8.2% for October to December 2026 and revised every quarter, is added every 31 March and is tax-free. Deposits also count under section 80C in the old tax regime.
When she turns 18 or passes Class 10, up to half of the balance can be withdrawn for higher studies with the admission letter or fee slip.
At 21 years from opening, or at her marriage after 18, fill the closure form and the full amount is paid into her bank account.
1800-266-6868 (India Post customer care); your bank branch if the account is with a bank
PM SVANidhi (Street Vendor Loan)
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, with SIDBI

A working-capital loan for street vendors with no collateral: Rs.15,000 first, then Rs.25,000 and Rs.50,000 once each loan is repaid. Repaying on time earns a 7% interest subsidy credited to your loan account, and taking and making payments by UPI or QR code earns cashback of up to Rs.1,600; vendors who repay the second loan can get a UPI-linked RuPay credit card. The scheme was restructured and extended in August 2025, and loans are given till 31 March 2030. You can apply yourself on the portal, or through a CSC or your municipal office.
Loans of Rs.15,000, Rs.25,000 and Rs.50,000 without collateral, with 7% interest subsidy
Street vendor selling in a town or city, with a Certificate of Vending or ID card from the municipality or Town Vending Committee
Or named in the municipality's vendor survey (Survey Reference Number), even if no certificate was issued
Vendors left out of the survey, or from nearby villages and peri-urban areas who sell within town limits, can apply with a Letter of Recommendation (LoR) from the municipality
Without an LoR, you must be a member of a vendors' association or have received the one-time Covid assistance
The Rs.25,000 and Rs.50,000 loans are given only after the previous loan is fully repaid
